bullets.title: Quotes from the writings of John Steinbeck
bullets.note: John is a master, and his hilarious [_Travels with Charley: In Search of America_](https://www.amazon.com/Travels-Charley-Search-America-Steinbeck-ebook/dp/B001BC6GN6/ref=sr_1_1?crid=TP61DIA9MIOE&dchild=1&keywords=travels+with+charlie+by+john+steinbeck&qid=1624044735&sprefix=travels+with+%2Caps%2C183&sr=8-1) is one of my favorite reads of the last several years.

bullets.title: Ben Goldacre: Battling Bad Science
bullets.note: Description: “Every day there are news reports of new health advice, but how can you know if they’re right? Doctor and epidemiologist Ben Goldacre \[[@bengoldacre](https://twitter.com/bengoldacre)\] shows us, at high speed, the ways evidence can be distorted, from the blindingly obvious nutrition claims to the very subtle tricks of the pharmaceutical industry.” I loved Ben’s book [_Bad Science_](https://www.amazon.com/Bad-Science-Quacks-Pharma-Flacks-ebook/dp/B003VTZTU8/) so much that I put excerpts in the appendix of [_The 4-Hour Body_](https://www.amazon.com/Hour-Body-Uncommon-Incredible-Superhuman/dp/030746363X/ref=sr_1_1?dchild=1&keywords=the+4-hour+body&qid=1623855368&sr=8-1) with permission. If you’d like to further develop your critical thinking, see [Dr. Peter Attia](https://tim.blog/2021/06/08/peter-attia-2/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf)’s “[Studying Studies](https://peterattiamd.com/ns001/)” series.
